fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, but the verse points somewhere else. Paul writes, “…the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God.” (1 Corinthians 10:20). Then he adds, “And I do not want you to be participants with demons.” His worry is that they would be taking part in something that belongs to demons.

Jealousy is right, friend. Paul asks, “Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy?” (1 Corinthians 10:22). He asks it right after saying you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too (1 Corinthians 10:21). Then he follows with, “Are we stronger than He?” I think that's his point: nobody is strong enough to push the Lord and come out ahead, so sharing both tables is a risk not worth taking.

Mercy is a gentler word, friend, but Paul's question goes somewhere else. He asks, “Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy?” (1 Corinthians 10:22). It comes right after his words about the cup and the table of the Lord and of demons (1 Corinthians 10:21). Then he asks, “Are we stronger than He?” I think he's pointing back to Israel's history, where God was not pleased with most of them and they were struck down in the wilderness (1 Corinthians 10:5), so provoking the Lord is serious and nobody is stronger than He.
